questions_and_answers.question: Once an employer hires a worker as an employee, the employee must prove to the employer his or her identity and right to work in the United States through the completion of Form I-9, _____________________.
Immigration Reform and Control Act (IRCA)
questions_and_answers.answer: Prohibits employers from knowingly hiring unauthorized aliens or hiring individuals without completing the employment eligibility verification process. Requires all employers in the U.S. to use Form I-9, Employment Eligibility Verification. Prohibits discrimination based on national origin and citizenship or immigration status with respect to hiring, firing, and recruitment or referral for a fee.

questions_and_answers.question: Hey, could you please go over the major provisions of the Immigration Reform and Control Act (IRCA)?First, employers can't discriminate based on citizenship status or national origin. You can't ask for additional documentation if the documents reasonably appear genuine and reasonably refer to the person presenting them.Second, employers can't knowingly hire or recruit people who aren't authorized to work in the United States. The verification process is completing the I-9 form. The employee must complete it on the first day of employment. The employer must complete section 2 within three days of the employee's date of hire.Third, there are record keeping requirements. Employers must keep the I-9 form for three years after the date of hire or one year after the date of termination, whichever is later.What are some ways that employers should know or do to remain compliant?Thank you!!
